```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
options(digits=2)
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
require(lubridate)
kRdata <- read.csv(file = 'kRdata.csv')
kRdata <- kRdata %>%
mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))
kData = kRdata
```
Data are from the Patient_Info dataset from South Korea 1 Jan to 1 May 2020. These data were retrieved from a downloadable zip file from kaggle.

Some of the data were uncoded for sex - sex must be just male or female.  77 of the data entries were coded sex as blank, so we omit these.  State of a patient must be died or alive - we adjust that as well.  This is done in the mutate function. 

Variables of interest: sex, result

Research Question: - Is dying independent of sex?

# Introduction

Using kdata, can we determine that sex is a factor in dying of Covid19?

$H_A$ There is a relationship between gender and death from covid 19 in Korea, 2019.

$H_O$ There is no relationship between gender and death from covid 19 in Korea, 2019.

# Methods

Sex is categorical. Result is catagorical.

# Data Results

## Graphical results    

```{r}
barchartGC(~result + sex,data=kData)
barchartGC(~result + sex,data=kData, type="percent")

```

The graph suggests that males are more likely to die from covid19 in comparison to females.


## Numerical results

```{r}
table1 <- xtabs(~result + sex, data=kData)
rowPerc(table1)
colPerc(table1)
```

The numerical results show that out of 100, 64% of males died compared to 36% of females, indicating that men are almost twice as likely to die from covid19 than women.


## Inferential results 

```{r}
chisq.test(table1)
chisqtestGC(table1)
fisher.test(table1)
```

The p value is 0.001, which is less than 0.05. This means we reject the null hypothesis and conclude that there is a connection between sex and death from covid19 in Korea,2019.


# Conclusions

To answer the question, can we determine that men and women are equally likely to die of covid19 from data collected in South Korea through May 2019?

We reject the null hypothesis and conclude that there is a realtionship between sex and death from covid19. The graphical summary shows that men have an increased likelihood of death compared to women. Futhermore, the odds ratio says that men die at a rate of 2.3 times more than the rate of which women die from covid 19.
